History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
28-year-old male with 6-week history of generalized fatigue, myalgias, and a transient calf rash after travel to the United States; blood tests and Lyme serology arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Feeling “aching all over,” tired and run-down for ~6 weeks.  
• Last felt well: Christmas/New Year; symptoms began ~mid-February, about 2 weeks after returning from U.S. holiday (end Jan–early Feb).  
• Course: Persistent; no clear improvement.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Mild decrease in appetite; no reported weight loss.  
  – Occasional mild headache; no visual changes, numbness, or tingling.  
  – Generalized joint aches (shoulders, back, hips, knees) without swelling.  
• Transient rash:  
  – Location: posterior calf.  
  – Onset: mid–late February; resolved over ~2 weeks.  
  – Minimal itch; noticed by wife; patient unaware of any bite.  
• Review of systems:  
  – No fever recalled (possible low-grade with sore throat).  
  – No sore throat currently, cough, dyspnea, chest pain, palpitations.  
  – No abdominal pain, dysphagia, reflux, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or hematochezia.  
  – No dysuria or hematuria.  
  – No other rashes or skin changes.  
  – Mood and stress presently good.  
• Functional impact: Attending work but with decreased concentration and reduced exercise tolerance.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – well controlled; no recent exacerbations.  
• Hay fever (allergic rhinitis).  
• No other chronic illnesses noted.

Medications:
• Preventative asthma inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (used morning and night).  
• Over-the-counter antihistamine – name/dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• Not documented.

Social History:
• Lives with wife.  
• Occupation: Works for a health technology company.  
• Smoking: Not clearly documented.  
• Alcohol: Occasional.  
• Recent travel: United States (late Jan–early Feb) with significant outdoor walking/hiking; wore shorts and boots.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• No examination findings recorded in transcript.  
• Vitals not documented.

Investigations:
• Planned:  
  – Blood tests: Complete blood count, renal panel, liver function tests, thyroid function, inflammatory markers.  
  – Lyme disease serology.  
  – Additional infectious/other screens as per clinician discretion (not specified).  
• No results available at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: Fatigue and generalized myalgias ×6 weeks
  • Differential includes post-viral fatigue, endocrine/metabolic causes, hematologic abnormalities, inflammatory conditions, and Lyme disease.
  • Plan:
    – Order comprehensive blood panel (CBC, U&E, LFT, TFT, inflammatory markers).
    – Review results via telephone follow-up ~1 week after testing.

Issue 2: Resolved calf rash suspicious for erythema migrans; possible Lyme disease
  • Plan:
    – Lyme serology included in blood tests.
    – If positive, commence appropriate course of antibiotics (e.g., doxycycline) per guideline.
    – Educate patient on signs of progression (neurologic symptoms, migratory arthralgia) and to seek care earlier if they occur.

Issue 3: Asthma – stable
  • Plan:
    – Continue preventative inhaler as prescribed; reinforce adherence.
    – No changes at present.

General Plan items:
• Provide support-line number for blood test booking.  
• Arrange telephone follow-up after results available.  
• Advise patient to return sooner if new or worsening symptoms develop (fever, expanding rash, joint swelling, neurologic changes).

● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional audio dropouts and unfinished sentences, but clinical content understandable.
